report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

What I ran: python -m pytest in the work folder. Result: 2 passed, 1 failed.
- test_plain: pass
- test_total: pass (399 with 10% off = 359.1, int() gives 359, the test expects 359)
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: FAIL, assert 959 == 960

Why it fails: cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction (truncates toward zero). It does not round.
1010 with 5% off = 959.5. int(959.5) = 959. The test expects half a cent to round up to 960.
test_total passes only because 359.1 truncates and rounds to the same number.
This is the same bug as the open TODO item "fix rounding in cart.total (customers see totals one cent short)".

Note for the fix: Python's round() rounds half to even (round(959.5) = 960, but round(958.5) = 958),
so it does not give "half rounds up" for every case. Floats can also land just under .5.
A safe way is integer math in cents, or decimal.Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP.

I changed no code. This answers the question only. Tell me if you want the fix made before tonight.
